title: Eventual successive quotient comparisons
statement: theorem coherentFormalModule_kernel_quotient_comparison_bound {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F H : CoherentFormalModule X I) (α : F ⟶ H) (c : ℕ) (S : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ X.Modules) (j : S ⟶ F.obj) (hc : ∀ (l m : ℕ) (h : m + c ≤ l), Subobject.mk (Abelian.image.ι (kernel.ι (α.hom.app (op l)) ≫ F.obj.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_add_right m c) h)).op)) = Subobject.mk (Abelian.image.ι (kernel.ι (α.hom.app (op (m + c))) ≫ F.obj.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_right m c)).op))) (hS : ∀ m : ℕ, ∃ e : S.obj (op m) ≅ Abelian.image (kernel.ι (α.hom.app (op (m + c))) ≫ F.obj.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_right m c)).op), e.hom ≫ Abelian.image.ι (kernel.ι (α.hom.app (op (m + c))) ≫ F.obj.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_right m c)).op) = j.app (op m)) : ∃ b : ℕ, ∀ d : ℕ, max c b ≤ d → ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ e : formalModuleQuotient I (n + 1) ((formalShiftedQuotient I S d).obj (op (n + 1))) ≅ (formalShiftedQuotient I S d).obj (op n), formalModuleQuotientπ I (n + 1) ((formalShiftedQuotient I S d).obj (op (n + 1))) ≫ e.hom = (formalShiftedQuotient I S d).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op

proof.text: On a finite affine open cover, use the coherent formal-module equivalence to identify alpha with a map f : M to N of finite modules over the completed Noetherian ring. Artin--Rees on its image identifies the eventual images in F_m with L/(L intersect I^(m+1) M), where L = ker f. Since hc stabilizes at m+c, and hS identifies its representative with j_m, these identifications hold for S_m and respect its transitions. Kernels and images are coherent, so the affine quotient-section calculation applies.

Artin--Rees on L in M gives an affine bound b for L intersect I^(r+b) M contained in I^r L. Take their maximum. For all d at least max(c,b), the explicit shifted quotient has affine sections L/I^(n+1) L. Its transition is the ordinary quotient transition, so taking its quotient by I^(n+1) gives the preceding term. These canonical comparisons are unique by their factorization equations with epimorphic projections; they agree on overlaps and glue to the asserted sheaf isomorphism.
